This file exists so that adding a surface is an ENTRY rather than a second
copy of a test. The join it feeds is the one that catches a silent no-op:
`chrome.send` to a message no installed handler registered reaches
DUMP_WILL_BE_NOTREACHED in WebUIImpl::ProcessWebUIMessage, which is fatal
in a DCHECK build and does NOTHING in the release build users get. Four
sections of astro://settings shipped in that state.
The floors are PER SURFACE and are not decoration. A scan that parsed
nothing reports the same clean verdict as a scan that parsed everything and
found no fault, so each surface states what its own healthy numbers look
like; a surface whose sends, listeners or declared messages fall below its
floor fails as `nothing was measured` rather than passing as `clean`.
Lower a floor only with the deletion that justifies it in the same change.
A floor that only ever descends is the gate switching itself off one
defensible step at a time — which is why these are written as the numbers
each surface actually has, not as round numbers below them.

surfaces.note: Fifteen upstream handlers adopted wholesale, plus SafetyHubHandler at global scope. The surface the scanner was written for.

One handler, ManagementUIHandler, installed through its static Create() rather than std::make_unique — the shape whose absence the scanner's vacuity denominator caught. min_events is 0 because the page subscribes to nothing: it asks seven questions once and renders the answers.
